label: Input token 0 or i at early original positions (t=2..5)
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires almost only during the original-input phase (99.6% of mass) when the current input is the digit 0 (56% of mass, 16x lift) or the letter i (36%, 12x lift), at original positions 2-5. It peaks at t=3 (48% of mass), and t=2 and t=4 are the next strongest. It never fires at t=0-1, at the delimiter, or (apart from a trace) in the copy phase. Weak secondary activations come from n, x and w at the same positions. The predicate covers 92% of activation mass but has only about 47% precision: roughly half of the 0/i inputs at these positions do not cross threshold, and no simple history variable we tried (prior digits, prior 0/i, previous token class, first occurrence, to_go) cleanly separates these. The strongest activations often come on a second consecutive 0 (e.g. s 0 0 0, f b 0 0), but that pattern does not explain them all.
